title: CP 121: hourly rates July 2026
summary: Gross hourly rates applicable from July 1, 2026, for 37 hours per week.
body: Waste: 3A 19.5145; 3B 19.3775; 3C 20.5325; 3D 21.0555; 3E 21.7190. Qualified window cleaners: 4A 19.3775 at entry; 4B 19.8540 after 8 months; 4C 20.1875 after 12 months; 4D 20.5235 after 18 months in the profession.

Category 5: apply the sector's collective agreement with minimum 1A; driver exclusively assigned to personnel transport 17.4160. Category 6 car wash 18.6565. Chimney sweeping: 7A 19.3775; 7B 19.8540 after 9 months; 7C 20.1875 after 17 months; 7D 20.5235 after 25 months.
Industrial cleaning: 8 without training 18.8680; 8A 20.0980; 8B and 8B1 20.4630; 8B2 21.0290; 8B3 21.5435; 8B4 22.1215; 8C 22.9920; 8F 21.0290. Categories 8D/8E follow CP 112, with minimum 8A.

title: CP 121: work minima and exceptions
summary: Sector minima are 18 hours per week and 3 hours per day. Categories 1A and 1B benefit from derogations; the general threshold is not 19 hours.
body: The sheet cites article 18 of the collective agreement of July 2, 2026 on work duration and organization, registered under number 200883/CO/121, effective January 1, 2026. It indicates minimum work of three hours per day and eighteen hours per week.

Work corresponding to categories 1A and 1B escape the weekly minimum. For these categories, the sheet also notes a derogation from the minimum three-hour duration of article 21 of the law of March 16, 1971 and from the one-third rule of article 11bis of the law of July 3, 1978. Check classification before setting a small schedule.

This practical sheet is a secondary source. The date indicated corresponds to the entry into force of the collective agreement it cites; use this reference when validating the contract by the payroll department.

title: CP 121: notice of schedule changes
summary: Variable part-time schedules require advance notice. The sector exception for unforeseen necessity requires worker agreement.
body: Since November 20, 2022, the standard legal notice period is seven working days. A mandatory collective agreement may provide another period, normally at least three working days. Report the applicable notice period in the work rules.

Articles 3 and 4 of the law of October 3, 2022 maintain certain old sector derogations until their expiration. For CP 121, derogation to less than three days concerns only unforeseen necessity with worker agreement. Check the applicable collective agreement before promising immediate availability in a job posting.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: CP 121: year-end bonus
summary: The Social Fund calculates the year-end bonus over a period from July to June. Check qualifying days and equivalent work before calculating the benefit.
body: The FGTB sheet updated March 2, 2026 notably provides for access after at least 60 actual or equivalent days during the period from July 1 of the preceding year to June 30 of the relevant year. Another path is based on a gross salary amount; the displayed threshold concerns 2025 and does not allow affirming the 2026 threshold.

The FGTB sector page https://www.accg.be/fr/secteur/nettoyage/salaires-et-indemnites/ouvriers/primes/prime-de-fin-d-annee confirms the standard rate of 9 % of reference salary and payment in December. For the 2026 bonus, the reference period is July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

Since the 2024 bonus, maternity leave is credited up to 114 days per leave, subject to actual work during the reference period. The Fund calculates the bonus; new members must follow the procedure for submitting the payment certificate to their union organization.

title: Social Fund: childcare assistance
summary: CP 121 provides for Social Fund assistance with childcare costs. Inform recruits of this benefit and documents to retain.
body: The collective agreement of November 29, 2023, made mandatory by royal decree of October 25, 2024 published December 11, 2024, adds childcare assistance to Social Fund benefits. Articles 42 to 47 inserted in the base collective agreement grant rights for costs from January 1, 2024, with first payment in 2025.

The assistance is 2 euros gross per day of childcare incurred and per child, for a maximum of 150 days per calendar year. It covers children until the year they turn 12. The worker must have performed duties under CP 121 during the relevant year.

A tax certificate must justify childcare in an approved facility or after-school program. Annual payment is based on the previous year's costs; the limitation period is three years after the end of the relevant year.
source: Federal Employment Service / Belgian Official Gazette · ejustice.just.fgov.be

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Window cleaning: height work and rope work
summary: The employer must justify access method choice by risk analysis. A window cleaner position on ropes requires rescue organization and appropriate training.
body: Book IV, Title 5, requires appropriate equipment and priority to collective protections. Articles IV.5-16 and IV.5-17 generally prohibit systematic or repetitive rope work. Exceptions require demonstrating that access by safer equipment is impossible or more risky, or that its implementation presents greater risks.

Article IV.5-18 notably requires two separately anchored ropes, a harness connected to a fall arrest device and specific training including rescue. No worker may intervene alone: another person must be able to alert quickly and know rescue procedures. A competent person designated by the employer supervises setup and work.
When recruiting, specify the techniques actually necessary and verify corresponding competencies. The last amendment mentioned in this title was published June 10, 2024.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Window cleaning: lifts and lift inspections
summary: Verify that lifting equipment is suitable for transporting people and that required inspections have been performed. Equipment designed only for loads is not a normal means of accessing windows.
body: Book IV, Title 4, of the Wellbeing Code regulates lifting. Using an apparatus designed for loads to lift people is only permitted in exceptional circumstances with risk analysis and corresponding regulatory measures.

Under articles 280 and 281 of the General Regulations recalled by the employment service, equipment meeting the regulatory definition of lifting apparatus must undergo inspection before first use then quarterly inspections by an external technical inspection service. Before site assignment, request applicable reports for the lift.
The reference date is the publication of the Wellbeing Code on June 2, 2017; the guidance page does not provide an update date.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Cleaning products: risks and training
summary: The employer must analyze product exposure before assigning staff. Provide instructions and protections appropriate to products actually used at the client site.
body: Articles VI.1-6 to VI.1-10 of the Code require chemical risk analysis. It must consider hazardous properties, supplier information, exposure routes and duration as well as working conditions. Include the position's cleaning and disinfection products.

Articles VI.1-15 and VI.1-16 prioritize elimination or replacement of the dangerous product, then technical and collective measures. Personal protective equipment is used when other means are insufficient.

Article VI.1-27 requires information and training, with access to safety data sheets. Article VI.1-28 addresses product identification in containers. Organize this onboarding before product use; the cited consolidation mentions an amendment published June 10, 2024.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Students: verify authorized cleaning tasks
summary: Student status does not automatically authorize dangerous tasks. Examine products, machinery and fall risks before proposing the position.
body: Risk analysis specific to young workers must precede work, be renewed annually and upon any position change. Plan the necessary onboarding, information and support, accounting for lack of experience.

Articles X.3-8 and X.3-11 of the Code frame dangerous work. For a student, the derogation notably requires at least 18 years of age, studies corresponding to the activities, effective preventive measures and the presence of an experienced worker. Prior advice from the prevention adviser and committee is also required.

Do not assign dangerous cleaning to a student based solely on reaching legal age. The date retained corresponds to the latest amendment mentioned by the Code title linked to this guidance, published June 10, 2024.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Students: written contract before starting
summary: Verify that studies are the candidate's main activity. A student replacement in cleaning requires a written individual contract before employment begins.
body: A student employment contract is concluded for a fixed term in two copies and signed no later than employment start. It must contain the mandatory terms of the student regime. Studies must be the main activity and work must remain secondary.

Continuous employment of at least twelve months with the same employer precludes using a student contract in that relationship thereafter. Also check exclusions related to education type and internships. Dimona formalities and safety obligations remain to be handled separately.

The date indicated is that of publication of the law of July 3, 1978 concerning employment contracts, which contains the student contract regime, namely August 22, 1978; the page provides no update date.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Cleaning at client: attendance recording
summary: Since September 1, 2024, affected real estate cleaning services require recording of start times, end times and breaks. Prepare system access as part of worker onboarding.
body: Check In and Out at Work applies to cleaning of real estate for a third party under work declaration conditions. Not all CP 121 activities are automatically covered. The employer informs staff of affected sites and provides recording means.
The worker records their presence in real time at the service location: IN at start, OUT at end, OUT when departing for break then IN when resuming. The employer cannot record attendance in advance.

Correction requires an employer request to the National Social Security Office, supported by documentation, within thirty days of recording. The legal basis appears in articles 22 to 49 of the program law of December 26, 2022. The page has news dated July 30, 2026.

title: Cleaning: declaration and recording thresholds
summary: The main contract amount and subcontracting determine the obligation. The NSSO FAQ clarifies thresholds and procedure when taking over a contract.
body: The October 15, 2025 employer FAQ confirms applicable thresholds: 30,000 euros without a subcontractor, 5,000 euros with one subcontractor and declaration even under 5,000 euros with at least two subcontractors. These thresholds are assessed excluding VAT for real estate work of the main contract.

CIaO recording applies to cleaning activities covered by the contract when work declaration is required, or when cleaning is added to an existing declaration. Check the main contract rather than just the cleaning worker's mission amount.
When a company takes over a client's contract, a new declaration must be filed. Communicate its number to workers, for example via a new QR code, to avoid recording under the old employer.

title: Cleaning: documents for social inspections
summary: The SIRS checklist of February 13, 2026 details documents checked at the company and on site. Verify work authorization and prepare supporting documents before assignment.
body: Prepare VAT and social security identification, employment registration, work rules, compensation data and contracts with amendments. For part-time workers, schedules and discrepancies must be verifiable; keep site declaration references and CIaO recordings.

Depending on the foreign worker's situation, verify applicable work and residence permits. In case of posting, prepare Limosa L1 declaration and A1 certificate. For a non-EU self-employed person, also verify the professional card where required.

On the client's site, staff must be able to identify their employer, status, schedule and compensation. Organize access to documents useful for inspection, including for students and temporary workers.
source: Social Information and Research Service · sirs.belgique.be

owner.name: Service d'information et de recherche sociale

title: Subcontractors: check debts before payment
summary: Real estate cleaning falls under tax and social debt checks on co-contractors. Non-compliance with withholding can engage joint liability.
body: The Finance Service requests checking the withholding obligation when concluding the contract then at each invoice payment. Use Check Withholding Obligation for the company executing cleaning or maintenance work.

When the check imposes withholding, it amounts to 15 % of the amount excluding VAT for tax debts and 35 % for social security debts. Pay the amounts to the relevant administration according to procedure. Transmit this verification to the supplier department before payment.

The official page, updated March 7, 2017 per its metadata, explains that respecting withholding protects against joint liability under legal conditions. These rates apply to tax and social security authorities; they do not describe the distinct mechanism for self-employed debts.

title: At client: avoid illegal worker provision
summary: A cleaning client cannot freely exercise employer authority over workers. Define in the service contract what instructions it can give.
body: Client instructions relating to wellbeing and safety are permitted. Other instructions must be explicitly detailed in a written agreement with the provider and cannot undermine its employer authority. Practice must respect this agreement.

The user must inform relevant negotiating bodies and provide, on request, the part of the agreement concerning instructions. Royal decree of July 17, 2013 organizes this information under article 31 of the law of July 24, 1987.

Illegal worker provision can create a permanent contract between the user and workers from the start of services. The user and provider are jointly liable for contributions, wages, indemnities and benefits concerned. For recruitment, clearly identify the employer and line manager.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Cleaning and service vouchers: choose the right commission
summary: A domestic help position under service vouchers does not automatically fall under CP 121. Check approval, employer activity and contract type before posting the salary.
body: A service voucher contract is concluded with a company approved by the competent Region. For a company employing only service voucher workers, the compensation of these workers falls under SCP 322.01. Service voucher workers from a temp agency also follow this SCP.

A sui generis section of a company with another activity may fall under the scales of the commission competent for that company. Administrative staff at a service voucher company do not automatically fall under SCP 322.01. The title 'cleaning' alone is therefore insufficient to choose the scale.

The weekly limit for SCP 322.01 is 38 hours according to this page. The date retained is publication of the founding law of service vouchers on August 11, 2001, absent an update date shown by the guidance.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: CP 121: Saturday, Sunday and night bonuses
summary: Base salary does not cover all off-schedule work. The collective agreement of February 5, 2026 sets the bonuses to budget for the position.
body: Articles 4 and 5 provide for a 100 % bonus of normal salary for Sunday or holiday work and 25 % for Saturday. The Saturday bonus does not apply to overtime already increased under the work duration collective agreement.

Article 3 provides for a bonus for work between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. If this work includes at least six hours and is preceded or followed by two hours of work, those two hours also qualify for the bonus. Category 8 has a specific regime to check.

The collective agreement enters into force January 1, 2026 and expires June 30, 2027, subject to its specific provision on scope. Hourly bonus amounts are indexable: use their value as of the date of work.
